run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:48:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert coincides with a short burst of HTTP 5xx errors on frontend-proxy's own ingress spans: the 5-minute error rate rose from 0.0037/s to a peak of 0.2259/s between ~23:48 and 23:55 and was back at 0.0074/s by 23:56. The burst is dominated by failed checkout calls: frontend spans POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, plus checkout's client spans oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, all errored at 0.08-0.22/s in the same windows, and frontend-proxy logged HTTP 500 'via_upstream' on POST /api/checkout. The failure therefore tracks back to the payment Charge call. Payment's Deployment was rolled out at 23:49:06Z with an unchanged pod template (same image, env, resources; only kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt added), and payment holds no readiness probe, so the old pod was removed at 23:49:09Z. The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config carries a switched-on fault setting paymentFailure with defaultVariant "100%" ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), which is the only fault-injecting setting that is on and refers to the restarted/failing dependency; all other fault flags read 'off'. However, the declared 100% charge failure itself was not observed: the new payment container logged 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' for sampled charges and checkout logged 'payment went through', so the conclusion stays partial and the setting-change history is unknown. frontend-proxy, frontend and checkout are affected on their own error evidence; payment itself shows no error spans and no error log lines, so it is implicated as the restarted dependency rather than shown as failing.

claims.text: frontend-proxy already carried a low background error rate before the alert and after the burst: 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0/s at 22:00-23:27, 0.0038-0.0222/s on points from 23:29 to 23:43, 0.0037/s at 23:49-23:50, then 0.0074-0.0083/s from 23:56 to 00:03.

The burst is visible in the 5-minute error rate of frontend-proxy spans: 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR went 0.0037/s at 23:50, 0.1481/s at 23:51, 0.2259/s at 23:52-23:54, 0.0852/s at 23:55 and 0.0074/s at 23:56; 'router frontend egress' error rate rose to 0.2185/s over the same window.

In the same window, frontend spans 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'POST' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' all had STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.1370/s at 23:51 and 0.2185/s at 23:52-23:54 and 0.0815/s at 23:55, while frontend 'GET', 'GET /api/cart', 'GET /api/data', 'POST /api/cart', 'tcp.connect' and the Ad/Cart gRPC client spans stayed at 0.

checkout's own spans 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' had STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.0934/s at 23:52, 0.0854/s at 23:53, 0.0819/s at 23:54 and 0.0815/s at 23:55, and 0 before and after; an instant reading at 23:53 gave 0.0854/s for both.

frontend-proxy's access log shows POST /api/checkout answered 500 'via_upstream' with a frontend upstream at 23:49:58.272, 23:49:58.972, 23:50:00.070 and 23:50:01.070, while a POST /api/checkout at 23:51:29.379 returned 200.

frontend-proxy's access log also records 503 responses with 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for GET /api/recommendations at 23:48:11, GET /api/products/0PUK6V6EV0 at 23:50:40, GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP at 23:51:39 and GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO at 23:53:29.

Before the alert, the sampled frontend-proxy error traces (23:30:55-23:35:50) are ingress spans with http.status_code 503 and otel.status_code ERROR, each with a 'router frontend egress' child carrying http.status_code "0" and a load-generator GET span with 503, i.e. the same upstream-reset pattern existed as background before 23:48.

Deployment payment in otel-demo was rolled out at 23:49:06-23:49:09: 'Scaled up replica set payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1' at 23:49:06, pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled 23:49:06, image already present + container Created 23:49:08, Started 23:49:09, RS 'Created pod: payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht' 23:49:06, and 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' with pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 'Stopping container payment' at 23:49:09.

The payment pod template was unchanged by that rollout: payment-55766d76b9 and payment-7b6bfb9fb4 both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with identical env (PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME=otel-collector, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES service.version=2.1.3), identical resources (cpu 20m/160Mi limits) and securityContext; the only template difference is the new RS's annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:49:06Z (new RS created 23:49:06, old RS created 23:16:07).

Deployment payment runs strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25% on 1 replica and defines no readiness probe (readinessProbe is null for its payment container); its status is 1 ready / 1 updated with condition NewReplicaSetAvailable since 23:49:09.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds demo.flagd.json with flag paymentFailure: description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', state ENABLED, defaultVariant "100%", variants {"100%":1, "off":0} - i.e. the value in effect is 1, not off/0.

Every other fault flag in the same demo.flagd.json reads defaultVariant "off": adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure.

The new payment container's log shows pairs of 'Charge request received.' immediately followed by 'Transaction complete.' at 23:52:10.926, 23:52:11.313, 23:52:13.466, 23:52:18.165, 23:52:22.857, 23:52:27.281 and further through 23:52:59, and 'Charge request received.' lines continue at 23:57:12-23:59:16.
checkout's log records 'payment went through' continuously from 23:55:25.685 to 23:56:59.928, and 'Successful to write message. offset: 0' Kafka writes from 23:53:58.336 to 23:54:58.491.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (flagd has two containers, both 0), frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94 were created 23:16:06/23:16:08 (before the incident), and payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht was created 23:49:06 under ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 with 0 restarts; all 21 otel-demo deployments report 1 ready / 1 available replica.

payment's own span error rate is 0 for all its listed operations (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect, grpc.flagd evaluation) both at 23:53 and at 00:05; nonzero error rates at 23:53 appear only on checkout's PaymentService/Charge + PlaceOrder, frontend's checkout-related spans, frontend-proxy ingress/egress, and small (~0.0037/s) flagd EventStream series on ad, recommendation and fraud-detection.

The only cluster events tied to otel-demo in the window are Deployment 'payment' ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 SuccessfulCreate, ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 SuccessfulDelete and pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started plus pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 Killing, all 23:49:06-23:49:09; the other event groups (Pod FailedScheduling 2, PVC Provisioning/WaitForFirstConsumer, Job Completed/SuccessfulCreate, StatefulSet SuccessfulCreate, PV VolumeFailedDelete) are in namespace data-recorders.

The switched-on flagd-config setting paymentFailure="100%" is the fault behind the burst: it names the payment service, payment was restarted at 23:49:06 with an unchanged pod template, no other object was observed applying a change or fault to payment, and the only failing call path in the traces/metrics runs through checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge.

Alternatively or additionally, the 23:49:06 rollout of the single-replica payment Deployment with no readiness probe may itself have broken checkout's in-flight gRPC Charge connections: the old pod was stopped at 23:49:09 while the replacement container had just started, and the Charge error burst (5m rate 0.08-0.09/s in the windows ending 23:52-23:55) and frontend-proxy 500s on /api/checkout (23:49:58-23:50:01) fall inside that interval.

Because the alert condition is an error rate above 0 and frontend-proxy carried sporadic 503 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' errors around the noted 23:48:49 threshold (logged at 23:48:11, 0.0037/s readings at 23:49-23:50, error traces at 23:30-23:35), the alert may have first fired on that background error rather than on the larger 23:48-23:55 check-out burst.

The declared 100% charge failure was not observed on payment itself: after the restart the payment container logged 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs (23:52:10-23:52:59) and charge receipts through 23:59:16, checkout logged 'payment went through' from 23:55:25 onward, and payment had no nonzero error-span rate at 23:53 or 00:05 - so payment was completing charges while the flag still read "100%" and while the burst was ending.

A crash, OOMKill, eviction or lost readiness of frontend, checkout or frontend-proxy is rejected as the cause: all otel-demo pods (including frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc, checkout-5dccddf8bb-c4dqt, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94) are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and were created 23:16:06-23:16:08, well before the alert, with no OOMKilled/Evicted event in the otel-demo event list.

The other injected-fault candidates are rejected as the driver of this burst: adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all read "off", and at 23:53 and 00:05 no error-rate burst appeared on ad, cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, email, accounting or fraud-detection beyond ~0.0037/s flagd EventStream noise.

Add a readiness probe to the payment container and, for a single-replica dependency, verify that the rollout keeps the old pod until the new one actually serves traffic (or allow maxSurge with a readiness gate), since the observed rollout at 23:49:06 removed the old payment pod 3s after the new one started with no readiness probe defined.

Re-read the flagd-config value for paymentFailure (currently "100%") and the flagd change history with a change-history integration, to establish whether it was set to "100%" around 23:48-23:49 and when it was reverted or bypassed, before attributing the burst to it.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not present in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with match {alertname="RequestErrorRate"} both returned no_data, so the alert expression, its evaluation window and its reported current value 0.0111 could not be verified.

Jaeger returned no traces for the incident interval (traces_search for checkout 23:45-23:58 and traces_search_by_tags error=true / otel.status_code="ERROR" for 23:45-23:58 all returned no_data; the only error trace sample covered 23:30:55-23:35:50), so checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span status message cannot be read and a gRPC status error cannot be distinguished from a transport/connection error.
The old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 was deleted at 23:49:09 and its logs are unavailable, so payment's behaviour between the alert start 23:48:49 and the restart 23:49:06 is unknown.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what set paymentFailure to "100%" in flagd-config, when it changed, and who issued the kubectl rollout restart (restartedAt 23:49:06) are unknown; the declared 100% charge failure was not observed directly.

Queries for payment log lines matching fail|error|warn|declin|abort over 23:49-00:10 and 23:49:10-23:50:30 returned no_data (no matching lines in the read slice), so the absence of payment failure log lines is unknown rather than established.

The frontend container's logs returned no lines for 23:30-23:55 (status no_data) and app_payment_transactions_total / http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series, so frontend's own error text and payment transaction counters could not be used.

Node-level resource state, networkpolicies, services/endpoints history and resourcequotas in otel-demo were not checked; a transient connectivity cause on the payment Service/endpoints path cannot be excluded.
next_steps: Review flagd/flagd-ui audit or change records and Kubernetes audit logs for flagd-config edits (paymentFailure) and for the payment Deployment rollout at 2026-11-17T23:49:06Z.
Capture a retained trace of a failing checkout PlaceOrder/PaymentService/Charge call during 23:48-23:55 (longer Jaeger retention or collector export) to read the gRPC status and error message.
Verify from the flagd-config history whether paymentFailure was "100%" during 23:48-23:55 and whether payment honoured it; compare with payment's charge success counters if they are exported.
Add a readiness probe to the payment container and confirm the rollout strategy avoids removing the only serving pod before the replacement is ready.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

view.span_groups_note: span_groups summarizes the spans shown in content; spans the adapter sampled out are not counted in any group.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
